title: APIs around ML Models
interviewAnswer: An API validates requests, invokes preprocessing and inference, then returns predictions or a job ID. Keep model logic separate from transport/UI so each layer can scale and evolve independently.
why: APIs are a common interface around online ML services and force you to think about schemas, validation, latency and failures.
intuition: The API receives a request, validates it, runs or submits inference, and returns a stable response contract without exposing model internals.
deepDive: Define versioned request/response schemas, authentication, size limits, timeouts and error codes. Load the model at process startup, not per request. Real-time inference should keep handlers short; long jobs should return a job ID and run asynchronously. Separate transport/API logic from preprocessing/model code to enable tests and alternative serving modes.
workedExample: POST /predict accepts validated tabular features and returns probability + model_version. POST /reconstruct accepts a file, returns job_id, and the client polls /jobs/{id}.
commonMistakes: Loading the model on every request.
Using synchronous HTTP for multi-minute GPU jobs.
followUps: How do you version an API?
production: Monitor request rate, p95/p99 latency, errors, payload sizes and model version. Add health/readiness endpoints and graceful shutdown for rolling deployments.
